examples.japanese: {多|おお}くの{苦難|くなん}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えてきた。
{苦難|くなん}の{時代|じだい}を{生|い}き{抜|ぬ}いた{人々|ひとびと}の{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.english: I listened to the stories of people who lived through times of adversity.

examples.japanese: {苦難|くなん}に{立|た}ち{向|む}かう{勇気|ゆうき}を{持|も}つことが{人|ひと}を{成長|せいちょう}させる。
examples.english: Having the courage to face adversity helps a person grow.

notes:
A somewhat literary word for serious suffering or difficult circumstances. Composed of {苦|く} (suffering) and {難|なん} (difficulty). Carries a weightier tone than casual words for difficulty, often used to describe prolonged or significant challenges that test character.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苦難|くなん}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}える: overcome hardship
- {苦難|くなん}に{立|た}ち{向|む}かう: face adversity
- {苦難|くなん}の{道|みち}: a path of hardship
- {苦難|くなん}に{耐|た}える: endure hardship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {困難|こんなん}: difficulty — more neutral, used for problems and obstacles in general
- {苦労|くろう}: hardship, trouble — more everyday, often includes personal effort
- {試練|しれん}: trial, ordeal — emphasizes the testing or challenging aspect
